title: Superhuman pushes its Go assistant everywhere
lede: Superhuman, formerly Grammarly, is making its Go assistant the central agent across its products, with cross-app context, proactive drafting, and Go agents running natively in Docs and Mail.

points: Go now learns context across connected apps, picks up each user's writing style and suggests personalised prompts; onboarding asks users to connect tools upfront.
It works inline at the cursor, manages other agents, and acts proactively by watching the calendar and inbox and drafting replies.
Twenty new connected agents arrive through the Go SDK, including DeepL, Legora, Amplitude, Databricks and Blackboard.
In Docs, agents run tasks in the background and routines fire on events; in Mail, Go replaces the old AI and handles enterprise search and inbox sorting.
After buying Fathom, Superhuman adds live shared notetaking, and Go can draft follow-ups such as a proposal after a meeting.

sections.text: The Go SDK is the route for third-party agents into Superhuman's apps, and CEO Shishir Mehrotra says Go already has over 1 million active users.
